title: bonsai.log/1
description: The log record (contract §8.1): one JSON line, at most 2,048 bytes, per thing an agent did or Bonsai recorded (a tool call, a guard decision, a ladder result, an ask, an outside event, a cleaned file). Records are appended whole to the main checkout's .bonsai/local/log/ (s-<session>.ndjson per session, w-<YYYY-MM-DD>.ndjson outside one), never committed, redacted as written. Written by Bonsai's recorder (the hooks) and its own commands; read by bonsai logs and the studio's forwarder (Bonsai has no screens of its own). A writer writes every field below, in this order, null where it does not apply (contract §2.2, §2.5); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one, and refuses a duplicate key. The last two fields, bonsai_path and bonsai_sha256, name the bonsai binary that wrote a session's records (spec §16 row 27); they are the names the guard has written since part 5, added to the schema in set 6.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2). Today's spool wrote v: 1.

id.description: A UUID for the record; a replayed line with the same id is a duplicate.

at.description: When it happened: ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds.

workspace.description: The workspace id from bonsai.yaml (contract §3): ws- and 26 lowercase base32 characters. The bridge maps it to the studio's project id. Today's spool field: project.

session.description: The agent's session id, or null outside a session (an outside event, a command run by hand).

agent.description: The agent program: claude-code today (contract §2.7); null for a record no agent made.

agent_event.description: The agent's own event name (contract §8.3), such as Claude Code's PostToolUse; null for Bonsai's own records. Today's spool field: event.

event.description: Bonsai's event name (contract §8.2). An open list: its known words, one line each on what they mean, live in Bonsai's one table of log events, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.log prints (and the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md, lists); this schema does not copy them, and a reader shows a word it does not know as other.

subagent_id.description: Claude Code only: the subagent that acted, or null. Today's spool field: agent_id.

subagent_type.description: Claude Code only: the subagent's type, or null. Today's spool field: agent_type.

tool_use_id.description: Claude Code only: the tool call's id, pairing its start and end records; null when no tool call.

input_hash.description: Pairs a call's start and end records without keeping its input: as today, the first 16 hex characters of an HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by the machine's salt. null when no tool call.

checkout.description: The working tree's folder name, never its path (contract §2.6). Today's spool field: worktree.

branch.description: The working tree's branch, or null.

task.description: The task the session's environment names (BONSAI_TASK), raw, as given and redacted like every free-text field; null when unset. The recorder decides nothing from it. Today's spool field: task_env.

role.description: The role the session's environment names (BONSAI_ROLE), raw, as given and redacted like every free-text field; null when unset. Today's spool field: role_env.

category.description: The tool's category (contract §8.2). An open list: its known words live in Bonsai's one table of log categories, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.log prints (and the reference page of lists lists); this schema does not copy them. A pack's own categories are written <namespace>.<Name>, and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. null when no tool.

target.description: What the tool acted on, redacted, at most 200 characters; a path outside the checkout is null, never written. For session_start and subagent_start the active task the recorder found (contract §13), or null; for clean the project-relative path deleted; for ask the ask's key.

ok.description: Whether the call succeeded (true), failed (false), or null when that does not apply.

kind.description: What kind of the event it is, or null: a prompt's user or task-notification; a failure's interrupt or error; a notice's type (Claude Code's notification type); for an ask record, its op (file, resolve or answer).

text.description: Short text, redacted, at most 300 characters: a notice's message, or an ask record's question; never the words of a prompt (a prompt record's text is null). null where it does not apply.
examples: Claude is waiting for your input

source.description: As today: where a session started from (Claude Code's SessionStart source), or null.

model.description: As today: the session's model, as the agent names it, or null.

reason.description: As today: why a session ended (Claude Code's SessionEnd reason); for clean, the rule that cleaned the file (contract §8.2); or null.

decision.description: For a guard record: allow or deny; null otherwise.

rule.description: For a guard record: the name of the rule that decided; null otherwise.

labels.description: For an event record only: the outside event's labels (contract §8.4), checked against the label definitions in force (the packs' declarations and the label files attached on this machine, not this machine's alone); {} otherwise.

remote.description: Claude Code only: the session's Remote Control id, never redacted, as today; null when none. Today's spool field: rc_session.

bonsai_path.description: The bonsai binary's own path, forward slashes, on a session_start record (written at every start) and on the guard record that made its log file; null elsewhere. Under the person's home folder it is written from a tilde and a slash, so no user name is in the log (contract §2.6); elsewhere as it is. The guard writes its absolute form until step 5.3 changes guard code, so no form is required here. Added in set 6, an addition (spec §16 row 27; the name is the one the guard has written since part 5).

bonsai_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bonsai binary at bonsai_path, 64 lower-case hex characters, on a session_start record (hashed at every start, so a binary swapped between a session and its resume is seen) and on the guard record that made its log file; null elsewhere. Added in set 6, an addition (spec §16 row 27).
